newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt meets unions to discuss 1997 budget.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt meets unions to discuss 1997 budget.

text.p: The Italian government met union leaders on Monday to discuss the 1997 budget and a metalworkers' dispute to try to avert the threat of a strike, political sources said.

The draft law, which aims to strip 62.5 trillion lire ($41 billion) from next year's projected public sector deficit, was passed by the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) at the weekend but union leaders remain opposed to some parts of the plan.
The centre-right opposition, which walked out of the budget debate in the Chamber, staged fresh protests across Italy on Sunday agaisnt the austerity plan.
Union leaders have said they want clarification of a proposed "Euro-tax" designed to raise 12.5 trillion lire and help Italy qualify at the outset for a European single currency.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi was joined for the talks by Deputy Prime Minister Walter Veltroni, Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi, Labour Minister Tiziano Treu and Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco.

Italy's three main union confederations took part in the talks and Giorgio Fossa, chairman of employers' confederation Confindustria, also arrived. But it was not immediately clear whether all three sides were sitting round the table together.

Union leaders are concerned that measures to stimulate job creation are lacking from the draft budget. They also want progress on renewing contracts for metal workers which lapsed in June. The workers have scheduled a strike on November 22, which would be their second such action in two months.

A senior member of the CGIL union, Guglielmo Epifani, said on Friday that without progress from the government on jobs, tax and the metal workers, union leaders would have no option but to "call workers out to fight".
